newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ciba SC shares gain on first trading day.
newsitem.headline: Ciba SC shares gain on first trading day.

text.p: Shares of Ciba Specialty Holding Inc powered higher on their first day of trading on Thursday, crowning one of Europe's biggest spin-offs with solid gains against a generally weaker Swiss stock market.
Shares of Ciba SC, being spun off from pharmaceuticals giant Novartis, closed at 116.50 Swiss francs, comfortably above the 110-franc issue price set for its global stock offering.
Opening at 112.75, they dipped briefly, then surged to 118 before meeting profit-taking in an otherwise bearish market.
Dealers cited demand from British investors who sought shares to balance their portfolios in line with the weightings of the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).

Some Novartis shareholders who sold their subscription rights to Ciba SC thinking profit-taking would push prices lower at first also scrambled to take new positions, as did investors who failed to be allotted any shares.
A series of options on Ciba also helped to support prices, one dealer said, adding that retail business was not very large but tended to be on the buy side.

John Owen at co-lead organiser UBS said the big demand reflected trust in Ciba management, approval of its emphasis on shareholder value and investors' discovery of the specialty chemical sector, especially among U.S. buyers.

"This has attracted quite a big chunk of U.S. interest. For Clariant, not a single U.S. investor was there on day one," he said, referring to the special chemical company spun off by Sandoz AG as it merged with Ciba-Geigy into Novartis in 1996.
Although not as sexy as pharmaceuticals, specialty chemicals are not as cyclical as bulk chemicals and produce higher margins, he noted.

Ciba SC had 1996 sales of more than 6.7 billion francs from additives, consumer care chemicals, polymers, pigments and textile dyes. It is the world's leader in additives, whiteners, certain polymers and pigments. It is second in textile dyes.

The issue price valued the company at around 7.93 billion Swiss francs, reflecting surprisingly strong demand that kept prices well above the price range of 72 to 86 first indicated last month by a bank consortium handling the deal.
The consortium had offered on Monday night to buy the rights for 90 francs and allocated 3.01 million shares in the global offering.
Ciba SC Chairman Rolf Meyer told Reuters he was satisfied with demand that emerged during the rights trading period.
"We are very pleased at the interest both domestically and internationally, and obviously the good market conditions also helped," he said by telephone from Basle.
But he declined to forecast how the share price would perform. Analysts have said shares were fairly valued fundamentally at around 100 Swiss francs.

One syndication official forecast prices would creep higher because not all the demand was filled during the offer, but then investors would wait and see whether the company can meet its ambitious targets for profitability.

Subscription rights for Ciba SC, spun off via a one-for-one rights issue to Novartis shareholders, had closed at 103.50 francs on Tuesday. That valued shares at 113.50 francs given the 10-franc subscription charge.
The implied price/earnings ratio at that level for the rights put Ciba SC at a premium to Clariant and other specialty chemical companies in Europe.
Top managers are all sinking a year's pay into share schemes, accentuating their desire to push shareholder value.
"The work really starts now," said a banker at CSFB, co-lead organiser for the global offering.
Ciba SC plans to report first quarter results and unveil its opening balance sheet in early May. Meyer declined to comment on business developments so far in 1997.
